2014 Q4.bq: We increased our gold production outlook twice in 2014, and finished the year near the top end of our original guidance, even without adjusting for divestments.

2015 Q4.bq: Likewise, gold production was up 4% and above the midpoint of our guidance.

2018 Q2.gq: In summary, a global cost production and capital outlook is unchanged, and we remain on track to meet our commitments in 2018.

2019 Q3.gq: Our development capital outlook has been lowered to $550 million as increases for Nevada Gold Mines and Ahafo are offset by lower spend in North and South America.

2020 Q2.gq: Australian's 2020 production and cost outlook is unchanged, with approximately 1.2 million ounces and $900 per ounce AISC.

2020 Q4.gq: And in the fourth quarter, we were placed on positive outlook by Standard & Poor's and we were upgraded by Moody's to Baa1 credit rating further demonstrating our balance sheet strength.

2021 Q3.gq: We now expect to produce approximately 6 million ounces of gold just below our original guidance range, and we are reaffirming our original guidance of 1.3 million gold equivalent ounces from copper, silver, lead, and zinc.

2022 Q4.bq: Peñasquito delivered a strong fourth quarter, setting a new record in December for the tons we moved ex pit and exceeding our full year production guidance for the third consecutive year under the Newmont operating model.

2024 Q4.bq: As a result, we were able to exceed our production guidance by delivering 6.8 million ounces of gold and over 150,000 tons of copper last year, of which around 85% was produced from our go-forward core portfolio.

2025 Q2.bq: Our second-quarter operational results outperformed our previous expectations, effectively bookending the first half of the year and establishing a solid foundation for consistent delivery in the second half.
